home.heroTitle: Stay inside the landmark everyone photographs
home.heroSub: You are not staying near Oranjestad. You are staying inside it — in the pastel Dutch-colonial block on the waterfront, above the vaulted arcade of arched windows and green-and-white tile.
home.beachHonest: An honest word about the beach: this is not beachfront. Surfside Beach is a 15-minute walk, Eagle Beach a 10-minute drive. What you get instead is the city — dinner on foot every night, the harbour from the pool deck, and the building the cruise passengers photograph.

home.factsTitle: Three things most visitors don't know
home.fact1: Aruba sits outside the hurricane belt. A date booked 12 months out is safe in a way most of the Caribbean cannot promise.
home.fact2: Aruba prices in US dollars. There is no currency surprise anywhere on the island.
home.fact3: Queen Beatrix airport has US preclearance — you clear US customs in Aruba and land home as a domestic passenger.

building.title: Casa Playa — the building
building.p1: Casa Playa is the former Royal Plaza Mall: the pastel Dutch-colonial block on the Oranjestad waterfront that fills a full city block facing the cruise port. In 2024 it was converted into 62 private residences above its vaulted arcade — the one with the fan-muntin arched windows and the green-and-white cement tile you'll recognise from every photo of Oranjestad.
building.p2: Residents get what the mall's architecture always promised: a third-floor pool looking over the harbour, a gym, a quiet library, valet parking under the building and security at the door around the clock.
building.p3: Walking in for the first time is a strange, lovely moment — you've seen this building before, on postcards and cruise-ship photo reels. Now your key opens it.

items.q: What taxes and levies will I pay?
items.a: Aruba charges a 12.5% tourist levy on vacation rentals, calculated on your total including the cleaning fee, plus a US$3 per night environmental levy. Both are itemised in your total before you pay — the price you see at checkout is final.

items.q: When can I check in and out?
items.a: Check-in from 3:00 PM to 10:00 PM, checkout by 11:00 AM. Early check-in (from 11 AM) or late checkout (until 3 PM) is $45 USD when the calendar allows — ideal before a cruise.
Yes — valet parking under the building, included with your stay. The entrance is on the back street, off the boulevard.

items.q: How fast is the Wi-Fi, really?
items.a: Measured at 100+ Mbps down. There's a dedicated desk in the living room. Remote workers regularly stay a month.

items.q: Can you walk to a beach?
items.a: Honestly: this is a city stay, not beachfront. Surfside Beach is about 15 minutes on foot along the waterfront; Eagle Beach — one of the Caribbean's best — is a 10-minute drive or short bus ride. If you want to step from your room onto sand, a Palm Beach resort will suit you better; if you want to walk to dinner, you're in the right place.

items.q: How far is the cruise terminal?
items.a: About 400 metres — a 5-minute walk with luggage. You can see ships in port from the corner of the building. Many guests stay the night before embarkation.
Full refund up to 14 days before check-in, 50% up to 7 days before. It's also shown on the booking page before you pay.

The building has an elevator from the garage and street level to the second floor, and the apartment is step-free inside. The shower is a walk-in with a low threshold. Tell us what you need and we'll answer precisely.

items.q: Do I need to pay in florin?
items.a: No. Aruba prices in US dollars everywhere, and so do we. Cards are accepted island-wide.

items.q: Can groceries be in the fridge when I arrive?
items.a: Yes — add the welcome grocery pack ($85 USD) when you book: coffee, milk, eggs, fresh bread, seasonal fruit and 12 bottles of water, waiting in the fridge.
